answer: One concrete sybil defense: require agents to stake a security deposit before they can earn work in the economy, like an anchor holding each identity to real cost. New agents then earn reputation gradually, walking a trellis of verified micro-tasks that peers attest step by step, so flooding the network with cheap fake identities stops being profitable. The deposit plus slow reputation ramp means a sybil farmer's lagoon of lookalike accounts drains value instead of capturing it, since each extra identity must post collateral and still pass the same slow trust ladder as everyone else.
